instruction:
Create comprehensive API interface specifications for the Economic/Political Discussion Board system. Generate OpenAPI 3.0 schemas and TypeScript/NestJS code for the following modules:

## User Authentication & Profile APIs

### Authentication
- POST /auth/register - User registration with email and password
- POST /auth/login - User login with email and password
- POST /auth/logout - User logout
- POST /auth/change-password - Change user password
- POST /auth/request-admin - Submit administrator request with reason

### User Profile
- GET /users/me - Get current user's profile
- GET /users/:id - Get user profile by ID
- GET /users/:id/articles - Get user's articles
- GET /users/:id/comments - Get user's comments
- PUT /users/me - Update current user's profile (display_name, bio)
- DELETE /users/me - Delete current user's account

### Administrator Management
- GET /admin/requests - Get pending administrator requests (super admin only)
- PATCH /admin/requests/:id/approve - Approve administrator request (super admin only)
- PATCH /admin/requests/:id/reject - Reject administrator request (super admin only)
- PATCH /admin/roles/:userId/promote-super - Promote to super admin (super admin only)
- PATCH /admin/roles/:userId/demote-super - Demote super admin to regular admin (super admin only)
- GET /admin/banned-users - Get list of banned users (admin only)
- PATCH /admin/bans/:userId/ban - Ban a user with reason (admin only)
- PATCH /admin/bans/:userId/unban - Unban a user (admin only)

## Section APIs

- GET /sections - List all sections
- GET /sections/:id - Get section details
- POST /sections - Create a new section (admin only)
  - Body: { name: string, description: string }
- PUT /sections/:id - Update section (admin only)
  - Body: { name?: string, description?: string }
- DELETE /sections/:id - Delete section (admin only)

## Article APIs

- GET /sections/:sectionId/articles - List articles in a section (paginated)
  - Query params: page?, limit?, sort? (newest|oldest), search?, tags?
- GET /sections/:sectionId/articles/:articleId - Get article details
- POST /sections/:sectionId/articles - Create article
  - Body: { title: string, content: string, tagList?: string[], attachments?: FileUpload[] }
- PUT /sections/:sectionId/articles/:articleId - Update article (owner only)
  - Body: { title?: string, content?: string, tagList?: string[], addAttachments?: FileUpload[], removeAttachments?: string[] }
- DELETE /sections/:sectionId/articles/:articleId - Delete article (owner or admin only)

## Article Attachment APIs

- GET /articles/:articleId/attachments/:attachmentId/download - Download attachment

## Comment APIs

- GET /articles/:articleId/comments - List comments for an article (paginated)
- POST /articles/:articleId/comments - Create comment
  - Body: { content: string }
- PUT /comments/:commentId - Update comment (owner only)
  - Body: { content: string }
- DELETE /comments/:commentId - Delete comment (owner or admin only)

## Search APIs

- GET /search/articles - Search articles
  - Query params: q (search query), page?, limit?, tags? (comma-separated list)

## Technical Requirements

### Pagination Pattern
All list endpoints should support pagination with:
- page: number (default: 1)
- limit: number (default: 10, max: 100)
- Response should include: data[], meta: { currentPage, limit, totalItems, totalPages }

### Sorting Options
- newest: sort by createdAt DESC
- oldest: sort by createdAt ASC

### Tag System
- Tags are free text, comma-separated in requests
- Tags should be normalized (lowercase, trimmed)
- Search should match any tag in the list

### Error Responses
Standard error format:
```typescript
{
  statusCode: number,
  message: string,
  error: string
}
```

### Authentication
- Protected endpoints require Bearer token
- Authorization checks based on user roles and ownership

operations.description:
Member registration endpoint that creates a new member account with email and password credentials.

## Purpose
This operation allows unauthenticated users to register as members of the discussion board system. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new member account with the provided email address and securely hashed password. The operation validates email uniqueness, password strength requirements, and optionally verifies the email address during registration based on the email_verified field in the database schema.

## Security Implementation
The implementation uses industry-standard password hashing algorithms to ensure password security. The email field must be unique across all member accounts, and the system validates this constraint before creating new registrations. The email_verified field tracks whether the user has verified their email address, which may be set during registration or through a separate verification workflow.

## Integration Context
This registration flow integrates with the member authentication system defined in the discussion_board_members table schema. The created member will have access to all standard member capabilities including creating articles, writing comments, and managing their profile according to the authorization requirements specified in the user actors documentation.

Implement JWT-based registration flow:
1. Validate input fields (email format, password strength)
2. Check email uniqueness in discussion_board_members table

4. Create member record with email_verified field set (true if immediate verification enabled, false if email verification flow required)
5. Generate access token and refresh token

operations.description:
Member authentication endpoint that validates email and password credentials to establish a secure session.

## Purpose
This operation allows registered members to authenticate with their email address and password. Upon successful validation, the system generates JWT tokens that enable the member to access protected endpoints and perform authenticated actions. The login operation verifies password correctness against the hashed password stored in the discussion_board_members table.

## Session Management
The system implements JWT-based session management using the discussion_board_member_sessions table to track active sessions. Each successful login creates a new session record with connection context including user agent, IP address, and timestamp information. The session tracking enables security monitoring and session invalidation capabilities.

## Security Considerations
The implementation includes brute force protection through rate limiting on failed login attempts. Suspicious activity triggers additional security measures including temporary account lockout and security notifications. The system logs all authentication events in the system logs for audit purposes.

operations.description:
Token refresh endpoint that renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

## Purpose
This operation allows members to obtain new access and refresh tokens without re-authenticating with their credentials. The system validates the provided refresh token against the discussion_board_member_sessions table and issues new tokens if the refresh token is valid and not expired. This enables seamless user experience across extended usage periods.

## Session Continuity
The refresh operation maintains session continuity by validating the existing refresh token and generating new tokens. This approach preserves the user's authenticated state while enhancing security through token rotation. The session information in discussion_board_member_sessions table is updated to reflect the token refresh.

## Security Implementation
Refresh tokens have longer expiration times than access tokens but can be invalidated through session termination. Suspicious refresh token usage triggers security alerts and may result in session invalidation. The system monitors refresh token patterns for anomaly detection.

3. Verify refresh token is not expired

5. Generate new access token and refresh token
6. Update session record with new refresh token

operations.description:
Administrator registration endpoint that creates a new admin account in the discussion board system.

## Purpose and Overview

This endpoint handles the registration of new administrator accounts for the discussion board platform. Unlike regular member registration, this endpoint is specifically designed for creating privileged administrative accounts with elevated permissions to manage content, users, and system configuration.

The registration process follows a secure multi-step workflow that ensures only legitimate users can gain administrative access. The operation creates an admin account linked to an existing member account and assigns appropriate role permissions.

## Security Considerations and User Permissions

### Authentication Requirements

- **Member Account Required**: The operation requires a valid member_id that references an existing user account
- **Admin Request Approval**: The member must have previously submitted and received approval for an administrator request
- **Role Assignment**: The admin_role_id references the specific permissions level being granted (regular admin or super admin)
- **Password Security**: Passwords must meet strong complexity requirements and are stored using bcrypt hashing

### Authorization Checks

- **Registration Authority**: Only authorized system components can create admin accounts (not user-facing)
- **Email Uniqueness**: Each admin email must be unique across the system
- **Role Hierarchy**: Super admin creation requires verification of current super admin privileges

## Relationship to Database Entities

### Primary Entity: discussion_board_admins

The operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_admins table with the following key fields:

- **id**: Unique UUID identifier for the admin account
- **member_id**: Reference to the source member account that requested admin privileges
- **admin_role_id**: Reference to the assigned admin role defining permissions level
- **display_name**: Admin's public display name from the member profile
- **email**: Contact email for notifications and administrative communications
- **password_hash**: Secure bcrypt hash of the admin's password
- **bio**: Optional biography or profile description
- **status**: Account status (active, inactive, suspended)
- **assigned_at**: Timestamp when admin privileges were granted

### Related Entities

#### discussion_board_admin_email_verifications

After admin account creation, an email verification record is created in discussion_board_admin_email_verifications:

- **admin_id**: Reference to the newly created admin account
- **token**: Cryptographically secure random token for email verification
- **expires_at**: Token expiration time (typically 24 hours from creation)
- **verified_at**: Timestamp when email is successfully verified (null initially)

#### discussion_board_admin_sessions

No initial session is created during registration, but subsequent login operations will create session records.

#### discussion_board_admin_password_resets

Password reset functionality is available through the discussion_board_admin_password_resets table but is not created during initial registration.

## Validation Rules and Business Logic

### Required Fields Validation

- **member_id**: Must reference an existing discussion_board_members record
- **admin_role_id**: Must reference an existing discussion_board_admins_roles record
- **display_name**: Required string field for admin identification
- **email**: Required valid email format with uniqueness constraint
- **password_hash**: Required secure password hash (bcrypt)

### Business Logic Validation

- **Email Uniqueness**: System checks for duplicate email addresses across all admin accounts
- **Role Validation**: Admin role must exist and be appropriate for admin creation
- **Member Status**: Source member account must be in good standing (not banned)
- **Request Status**: The corresponding admin request must be in approved status

### Security Validation

- **Password Strength**: Password must meet complexity requirements (minimum length, character diversity)
- **Email Format**: Email must be valid format and from approved domains if domain restrictions apply
- **IP Logging**: Registration IP and user agent should be logged for security auditing

## Implementation Details

### Service Layer Logic

1. **Input Validation**:
   - Verify member_id references existing active member
   - Verify admin_role_id references valid admin role
   - Validate email format and uniqueness
   - Check password strength requirements

2. **Admin Account Creation**:
   - Generate unique UUID for admin account
   - Create bcrypt hash of provided password
   - Create admin record with current timestamp for assigned_at
   - Set initial status to 'active' or 'pending_email_verification'

3. **Email Verification**:
   - Generate cryptographically secure random token
   - Create email verification record with token and expiration
   - Send verification email to admin email address

4. **Audit Logging**:
   - Log admin creation event with IP address and user agent
   - Record timestamp and source of admin request approval

### Database Queries

```typescript
// 1. Verify member exists and is in good standing
const member = await prisma.discussion_board_members.findUnique({
  where: { id: member_id },
  select: { id: true, banned: true, status: true }
});

// 2. Verify admin role exists
const adminRole = await prisma.discussion_board_admins_roles.findUnique({
  where: { id: admin_role_id }
});

// 3. Check email uniqueness
const existingAdmin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.findUnique({
  where: { email: email }
});

// 4. Create admin account
const admin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.create({
  data: {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    member_id,
    admin_role_id,
    display_name,
    email,
    password_hash: bcrypt.hashSync(password, 10),
    bio: bio || null,
    status: 'active',
    assigned_at: new Date()
  }
});

// 5. Create email verification record
await prisma.discussion_board_admin_email_verifications.create({
  data: {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    admin_id: admin.id,
    token: crypto.randomUUID(),
    expires_at: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000), // 24 hours
    verified_at: null
  }
});
```

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **Email Already Exists**: Return 409 Conflict with descriptive error
2. **Invalid Member ID**: Return 404 Not Found
3. **Invalid Admin Role**: Return 404 Not Found
4. **Password Too Weak**: Return 400 Bad Request with strength requirements
5. **Member Banned**: Return 403 Forbidden
6. **Admin Request Not Approved**: Return 403 Forbidden

## Related Operations and Workflow Integration

### Dependent Operations

- **Member Account Verification**: Admin registration should only be available after member account is verified
- **Admin Request Approval**: Admin registration typically follows approval of an administrator request

### Sequential Operations

1. **User registers as member** → Member account created in discussion_board_members
2. **User submits admin request** → Request stored in discussion_board_admins_requests
3. **Super admin approves request** → Request status updated, admin eligible to register
4. **Admin account registration** → Admin account created in discussion_board_admins
5. **Email verification** → Admin confirms email ownership
6. **Admin login** → Session created in discussion_board_admin_sessions

## Security Considerations Within Schema Constraints

### Password Security

- Passwords are stored using bcrypt hashing with appropriate cost factor
- Password reset functionality available through discussion_board_admin_password_resets table
- No plain-text password storage or transmission

### Session Management

- No immediate session created during registration
- Admin must authenticate separately to create session
- All sessions tracked in discussion_board_admin_sessions for audit purposes

### Audit Trail

- Admin creation logged with IP address and user agent
- Timestamps track when admin privileges were assigned
- Email verification status tracked for security compliance

## Summary

This admin registration endpoint creates secure administrative accounts with appropriate permissions and integrates with the discussion board's comprehensive authentication and authorization system. The operation ensures only legitimate users with proper approval can gain administrative access while maintaining security best practices for password storage and session management.

Administrator authentication endpoint that validates admin credentials and establishes secure authentication sessions.

## Purpose and Overview

This endpoint handles the authentication of administrator accounts for the discussion board platform. It verifies admin credentials against the stored password hash, creates authentication sessions for security auditing, and returns JWT tokens for subsequent API authorization.

The authentication process implements industry-standard security practices including credential validation, session management, and audit logging to ensure the integrity and traceability of administrative access to the platform.

## Security Considerations and User Permissions

### Authentication Requirements

- **Admin Credentials**: Valid email address and password combination
- **Password Verification**: Password is verified against bcrypt-hashed password_hash in the database
- **Session Management**: Successful authentication creates session records in discussion_board_admin_sessions

- **Admin Account Status**: Admin account must be in active status (not banned or suspended)
- **Email Verification**: Admin must have verified their email address (verified_at field in discussion_board_admin_email_verifications)
- **Session Isolation**: Each login creates a distinct session with unique connection context

## Relationship to Database Entities

### Primary Entity: discussion_board_admins

The operation queries the discussion_board_admins table with the following key fields:

- **id**: Unique UUID identifier for the admin account
- **email**: Contact email used for authentication (with unique constraint)
- **password_hash**: bcrypt-hashed password for credential verification
- **status**: Account status must be 'active' for authentication
- **member_id**: Reference to the source member account
- **assigned_at**: Timestamp when admin privileges were granted

### Related Entities

#### discussion_board_admin_sessions

After successful authentication, a session record is created in discussion_board_admin_sessions:

- **admin_id**: Reference to the authenticated admin account
- **ip**: Client IP address for security auditing
- **href**: URL where authentication was initiated
- **referrer**: Referrer URL if applicable
- **created_at**: Timestamp when session was created
- **expired_at**: Session expiration time (JWT token validity period)

#### discussion_board_admin_email_verifications

The system verifies email verification status through the admin's email verification record:

- **verified_at**: Must be non-null for authentication to succeed
- **token**: Verification token (not directly used in login flow)
- **expires_at**: Token expiration for audit purposes

#### discussion_board_admin_password_resets

Password reset status can be checked through this table for security auditing, though not required for login:

- **used_at**: Tracks if recent password resets occurred
- **expires_at**: Password reset token expiration

## Validation Rules and Business Logic

### Required Fields Validation

- **email**: Required valid email format matching admin email
- **password**: Required string for credential verification

### Business Logic Validation

- **Email Uniqueness**: System validates that email exists in discussion_board_admins
- **Status Check**: Admin account must not be banned or suspended
- **Email Verification**: Admin must have completed email verification process
- **Password Matching**: bcrypt comparison of provided password against stored password_hash

### Security Validation

- **Rate Limiting**: Implement rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks
- **IP Logging**: Client IP address is logged for security auditing
- **User Agent Logging**: User agent string helps detect unauthorized access
- **Audit Trail**: All authentication attempts are logged for security monitoring

## Implementation Details

### Service Layer Logic

1. **Input Validation**:
   - Verify email format and existence in admin table
   - Validate password is provided and not empty

2. **Admin Lookup**:
   - Query discussion_board_admins by email with unique constraint
   - Verify admin account status is 'active'
   - Check email verification status

3. **Credential Verification**:
   - Compare bcrypt hash of provided password with stored password_hash
   - Handle failed authentication attempts

4. **Session Creation**:
   - Generate JWT access and refresh tokens
   - Create session record with connection context
   - Set appropriate expiration times

5. **Audit Logging**:
   - Log successful authentication with IP and user agent
   - Record timestamp and admin identifier

### Database Queries

```typescript
// 1. Find admin by email
const admin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.findUnique({
  where: { email: email },
  select: {
    id: true,
    email: true,
    password_hash: true,
    status: true,
    member_id: true
  }
});

// 2. Check email verification
const emailVerification = await prisma.discussion_board_admin_email_verifications.findFirst({
  where: {
    admin_id: admin.id,
    verified_at: { not: null }
  }
});

// 3. Verify password
const isPasswordValid = bcrypt.compareSync(password, admin.password_hash);

// 4. Create session
const session = await prisma.discussion_board_admin_sessions.create({
  data: {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    admin_id: admin.id,
    ip: clientIp,
    href: requestUrl,
    referrer: referrerUrl || null,
    created_at: new Date(),
    expired_at: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) // 24 hours
  }
});
```

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **Invalid Email**: Return 401 Unauthorized with generic error
2. **Invalid Password**: Return 401 Unauthorized with attempt logging
3. **Account Not Active**: Return 403 Forbidden with status explanation
4. **Email Not Verified**: Return 403 Forbidden requiring email verification
5. **Rate Limit Exceeded**: Return 429 Too Many Requests
6. **Session Creation Failure**: Return 500 Internal Server Error

## Related Operations and Workflow Integration

### Dependent Operations

- **Email Verification**: Must be completed before successful login
- **Session Invalidation**: Password change invalidates all existing sessions

### Sequential Operations

1. **Admin Registration** → Admin account created in discussion_board_admins
2. **Email Verification** → Email confirmed in discussion_board_admin_email_verifications
3. **Admin Login** → Session created in discussion_board_admin_sessions
4. **Session Refresh** → New tokens generated using refresh token
5. **Admin Logout** → Session terminated (client-side token discard)

### Parallel Operations

- **Profile Information**: Can be retrieved concurrently after authentication
- **Permission Check**: Admin role permissions verified per request

## Security Considerations Within Schema Constraints

### Password Security

- bcrypt hashing provides strong password protection
- Password reset functionality available for compromised accounts
- No password storage or transmission in plain text

### Session Management

- JWT tokens provide stateless authentication
- Session records enable security auditing and tracking
- Session expiration prevents unauthorized long-term access
- Password changes invalidate all sessions for security

### Audit Trail

- All login attempts logged with IP and user agent
- Session records provide detailed access tracking
- Timestamps enable security analysis and monitoring

## Summary

This admin authentication endpoint provides secure credential-based authentication for administrator accounts. The operation integrates with the discussion board's comprehensive session management and audit logging systems to ensure secure, traceable access to administrative features. All authentication activities are logged for security auditing and compliance purposes.

Administrator token refresh endpoint that issues new authentication tokens using refresh tokens.

## Purpose and Overview

This endpoint handles the refresh of authentication tokens for administrator accounts on the discussion board platform. It validates refresh tokens against active sessions, generates new JWT tokens (both access and refresh tokens), and maintains secure session management through token rotation.

The token refresh mechanism provides a balance between security and user experience by allowing extended authentication sessions while implementing security best practices like token rotation and expiration management.

## Security Considerations and User Permissions

### Token Refresh Requirements

- **Refresh Token Validation**: Valid refresh token must be provided in the request
- **Session Verification**: Refresh token must correspond to an active session in discussion_board_admin_sessions
- **Token Rotation**: New tokens are issued on each refresh to implement security best practices
- **Session Expiration**: Tokens cannot be refreshed after session expiration

### Authorization Checks

- **Active Session**: The session must not be expired (expired_at must be in the future)
- **Session Status**: Session must not be revoked or invalidated
- **Admin Account Status**: Associated admin account must remain in active status

## Relationship to Database Entities

### Primary Entity: discussion_board_admin_sessions

The operation queries and updates the discussion_board_admin_sessions table:

- **admin_id**: Reference to the admin account for the session
- **ip**: Client IP address (logged for security auditing)
- **href**: URL where session was initiated
- **referrer**: Referrer URL if applicable
- **created_at**: Session creation timestamp
- **expired_at**: Session expiration time (must be in future for refresh)

### Token Management

#### JWT Token Structure

The system generates two types of tokens:

- **Access Token**: Short-lived token (typically 1 hour) used for API authorization
- **Refresh Token**: Longer-lived token (typically 24 hours) used to obtain new access tokens

#### Token Storage

Tokens are not stored in the database for security reasons. Instead, the system:

- Validates refresh token format and signature
- Verifies token expiration against session expired_at
- Checks session validity against database records

## Validation Rules and Business Logic

### Required Fields Validation

- **refreshToken**: Required valid refresh token string
- **format**: Token must be properly formatted JWT token

### Business Logic Validation

- **Session Existence**: Refresh token must correspond to an active session
- **Expiration Check**: Session must not be expired (expired_at > current time)
- **Token Validity**: Refresh token must be cryptographically valid
- **Admin Status**: Admin account must not be banned or suspended

### Security Validation

- **Token Rotation**: New tokens issued on each refresh to prevent token theft
- **Session Integrity**: Session metadata updated to track refresh activities
- **Audit Logging**: All token refresh activities logged for security auditing

## Implementation Details

### Service Layer Logic

1. **Input Validation**:
   - Verify refresh token format and structure
   - Decode JWT token to extract payload
   - Validate token signature and expiration

2. **Session Verification**:
   - Query discussion_board_admin_sessions by admin_id from token
   - Verify session is not expired (expired_at > now)
   - Check admin account status

3. **Token Generation**:
   - Generate new access token with 1-hour expiration
   - Generate new refresh token with 24-hour expiration
   - Implement token rotation for security

4. **Session Update**:
   - Update session metadata if needed
   - Log refresh activity for audit trail

### Database Queries

```typescript
// 1. Decode and verify refresh token
const decoded = jwt.verify(refreshToken, process.env.JWT_SECRET);
const adminId = decoded.adminId;

// 2. Find active session
const session = await prisma.discussion_board_admin_sessions.findFirst({
  where: {
    admin_id: adminId,
    expired_at: { gt: new Date() }
  },
  orderBy: { created_at: 'desc' }
});

// 3. Verify admin status
const admin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.findUnique({
  where: { id: adminId },
  select: { status: true }
});

// 4. Generate new tokens
const newAccessToken = jwt.sign(
  { adminId, role: adminRole },
  process.env.JWT_SECRET,
  { expiresIn: '1h' }
);

const newRefreshToken = jwt.sign(
  { adminId },
  process.env.JWT_SECRET,
  { expiresIn: '24h' }
);
```

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **Invalid Refresh Token**: Return 401 Unauthorized
2. **Expired Session**: Return 401 Unauthorized with message to re-login
3. **Account Banned**: Return 403 Forbidden with explanation
4. **Session Not Found**: Return 401 Unauthorized
5. **Token Decode Failure**: Return 401 Unauthorized

## Related Operations and Workflow Integration

### Dependent Operations

- **Login Operation**: Initial authentication creates session and tokens
- **Logout Operation**: Invalidates session (client-side token discard)

### Sequential Operations

1. **Admin Login** → Initial tokens generated and session created
2. **API Requests** → Access token used for authorization
3. **Token Refresh** → New tokens issued using refresh token
4. **Repeat** → Steps 2-3 continue until session expires

### Parallel Operations

- **Profile Information**: Can be retrieved concurrently after token refresh
- **Permission Verification**: Admin role permissions checked per request

## Security Considerations Within Schema Constraints

### Token Security

- JWT tokens provide stateless authentication
- Token rotation implemented for security
- Refresh tokens have longer expiration but are rotated

### Session Management

- Session records in discussion_board_admin_sessions enable tracking
- Expiration times enforced at application level
- Admin status checked on each token refresh

### Audit Trail

- Token refresh activities logged for security auditing
- IP addresses and user agents tracked
- Timestamps enable security analysis

## Summary

The operation implements industry-standard token rotation practices while maintaining security through session validation and audit logging. The system balances convenience with security by allowing extended authentication sessions while protecting against token theft and unauthorized access.

operations.description:
Administrator registration endpoint that creates a new admin account in the discussion board system.

## Purpose and Overview

This endpoint handles the registration of new administrator accounts for the discussion board platform. Unlike regular member registration, this endpoint is specifically designed for creating privileged administrative accounts with elevated permissions to manage content, users, and system configuration.

The registration process follows a secure multi-step workflow that ensures only legitimate users can gain administrative access. The operation creates an admin account linked to an existing member account and assigns appropriate role permissions.

## Security Considerations and User Permissions

### Authentication Requirements

- **Member Account Required**: The operation requires a valid member_id that references an existing user account
- **Admin Request Approval**: The member must have previously submitted and received approval for an administrator request
- **Role Assignment**: The admin_role_id references the specific permissions level being granted (regular admin or super admin)
- **Password Security**: Passwords must meet strong complexity requirements and are stored using bcrypt hashing

### Authorization Checks

- **Registration Authority**: Only authorized system components can create admin accounts (not user-facing)
- **Email Uniqueness**: Each admin email must be unique across the system
- **Role Hierarchy**: Super admin creation requires verification of current super admin privileges

## Relationship to Database Entities

### Primary Entity: discussion_board_admins

The operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_admins table with the following key fields:

- **id**: Unique UUID identifier for the admin account
- **member_id**: Reference to the source member account that requested admin privileges
- **admin_role_id**: Reference to the assigned admin role defining permissions level
- **display_name**: Admin's public display name from the member profile
- **email**: Contact email for notifications and administrative communications
- **password_hash**: Secure bcrypt hash of the admin's password
- **bio**: Optional biography or profile description
- **status**: Account status (active, inactive, suspended)
- **assigned_at**: Timestamp when admin privileges were granted

### Related Entities

#### discussion_board_admin_email_verifications

After admin account creation, an email verification record is created in discussion_board_admin_email_verifications:

- **admin_id**: Reference to the newly created admin account
- **token**: Cryptographically secure random token for email verification
- **expires_at**: Token expiration time (typically 24 hours from creation)
- **verified_at**: Timestamp when email is successfully verified (null initially)

#### discussion_board_admin_sessions

No initial session is created during registration, but subsequent login operations will create session records.

#### discussion_board_admin_password_resets

Password reset functionality is available through the discussion_board_admin_password_resets table but is not created during initial registration.

## Validation Rules and Business Logic

### Required Fields Validation

- **member_id**: Must reference an existing discussion_board_members record
- **admin_role_id**: Must reference an existing discussion_board_admins_roles record
- **display_name**: Required string field for admin identification
- **email**: Required valid email format with uniqueness constraint
- **password_hash**: Required secure password hash (bcrypt)

### Business Logic Validation

- **Email Uniqueness**: System checks for duplicate email addresses across all admin accounts
- **Role Validation**: Admin role must exist and be appropriate for admin creation
- **Member Status**: Source member account must be in good standing (not banned)
- **Request Status**: The corresponding admin request must be in approved status

### Security Validation

- **Password Strength**: Password must meet complexity requirements (minimum length, character diversity)
- **Email Format**: Email must be valid format and from approved domains if domain restrictions apply
- **IP Logging**: Registration IP and user agent should be logged for security auditing

## Implementation Details

### Service Layer Logic

1. **Input Validation**:
   - Verify member_id references existing active member
   - Verify admin_role_id references valid admin role
   - Validate email format and uniqueness
   - Check password strength requirements

2. **Admin Account Creation**:
   - Generate unique UUID for admin account
   - Create bcrypt hash of provided password
   - Create admin record with current timestamp for assigned_at
   - Set initial status to 'active' or 'pending_email_verification'

3. **Email Verification**:
   - Generate cryptographically secure random token
   - Create email verification record with token and expiration
   - Send verification email to admin email address

4. **Audit Logging**:
   - Log admin creation event with IP address and user agent
   - Record timestamp and source of admin request approval

### Database Queries

```typescript
// 1. Verify member exists and is in good standing
const member = await prisma.discussion_board_members.findUnique({
  where: { id: member_id },
  select: { id: true, banned: true, status: true }
});

// 2. Verify admin role exists
const adminRole = await prisma.discussion_board_admins_roles.findUnique({
  where: { id: admin_role_id }
});

// 3. Check email uniqueness
const existingAdmin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.findUnique({
  where: { email: email }
});

// 4. Create admin account
const admin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.create({
  data: {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    member_id,
    admin_role_id,
    display_name,
    email,
    password_hash: bcrypt.hashSync(password, 10),
    bio: bio || null,
    status: 'active',
    assigned_at: new Date()
  }
});

// 5. Create email verification record
await prisma.discussion_board_admin_email_verifications.create({
  data: {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    admin_id: admin.id,
    token: crypto.randomUUID(),
    expires_at: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000), // 24 hours
    verified_at: null
  }
});
```

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **Email Already Exists**: Return 409 Conflict with descriptive error
2. **Invalid Member ID**: Return 404 Not Found
3. **Invalid Admin Role**: Return 404 Not Found
4. **Password Too Weak**: Return 400 Bad Request with strength requirements
5. **Member Banned**: Return 403 Forbidden
6. **Admin Request Not Approved**: Return 403 Forbidden

## Related Operations and Workflow Integration

### Dependent Operations

- **Member Account Verification**: Admin registration should only be available after member account is verified
- **Admin Request Approval**: Admin registration typically follows approval of an administrator request

### Sequential Operations

1. **User registers as member** → Member account created in discussion_board_members
2. **User submits admin request** → Request stored in discussion_board_admins_requests
3. **Super admin approves request** → Request status updated, admin eligible to register
4. **Admin account registration** → Admin account created in discussion_board_admins
5. **Email verification** → Admin confirms email ownership
6. **Admin login** → Session created in discussion_board_admin_sessions

## Security Considerations Within Schema Constraints

### Password Security

- Passwords are stored using bcrypt hashing with appropriate cost factor
- Password reset functionality available through discussion_board_admin_password_resets table
- No plain-text password storage or transmission

### Session Management

- No immediate session created during registration
- Admin must authenticate separately to create session
- All sessions tracked in discussion_board_admin_sessions for audit purposes

### Audit Trail

- Admin creation logged with IP address and user agent
- Timestamps track when admin privileges were assigned
- Email verification status tracked for security compliance

## Summary

This admin registration endpoint creates secure administrative accounts with appropriate permissions and integrates with the discussion board's comprehensive authentication and authorization system. The operation ensures only legitimate users with proper approval can gain administrative access while maintaining security best practices for password storage and session management.

operations.description:
Administrator token refresh endpoint that issues new authentication tokens using refresh tokens.

## Purpose and Overview

This endpoint handles the refresh of authentication tokens for administrator accounts on the discussion board platform. It validates refresh tokens against active sessions, generates new JWT tokens (both access and refresh tokens), and maintains secure session management through token rotation.

The token refresh mechanism provides a balance between security and user experience by allowing extended authentication sessions while implementing security best practices like token rotation and expiration management.

## Security Considerations and User Permissions

### Token Refresh Requirements

- **Refresh Token Validation**: Valid refresh token must be provided in the request
- **Session Verification**: Refresh token must correspond to an active session in discussion_board_admin_sessions
- **Token Rotation**: New tokens are issued on each refresh to implement security best practices
- **Session Expiration**: Tokens cannot be refreshed after session expiration

### Authorization Checks

- **Active Session**: The session must not be expired (expired_at must be in the future)
- **Session Status**: Session must not be revoked or invalidated
- **Admin Account Status**: Associated admin account must remain in active status

## Relationship to Database Entities

### Primary Entity: discussion_board_admin_sessions

The operation queries and updates the discussion_board_admin_sessions table:

- **admin_id**: Reference to the admin account for the session
- **ip**: Client IP address (logged for security auditing)
- **href**: URL where session was initiated
- **referrer**: Referrer URL if applicable
- **created_at**: Session creation timestamp
- **expired_at**: Session expiration time (must be in future for refresh)

### Token Management

#### JWT Token Structure

The system generates two types of tokens:

- **Access Token**: Short-lived token (typically 1 hour) used for API authorization
- **Refresh Token**: Longer-lived token (typically 24 hours) used to obtain new access tokens

#### Token Storage

Tokens are not stored in the database for security reasons. Instead, the system:

- Validates refresh token format and signature
- Verifies token expiration against session expired_at
- Checks session validity against database records

## Validation Rules and Business Logic

### Required Fields Validation

- **refreshToken**: Required valid refresh token string
- **format**: Token must be properly formatted JWT token

### Business Logic Validation

- **Session Existence**: Refresh token must correspond to an active session
- **Expiration Check**: Session must not be expired (expired_at > current time)
- **Token Validity**: Refresh token must be cryptographically valid
- **Admin Status**: Admin account must not be banned or suspended

### Security Validation

- **Token Rotation**: New tokens issued on each refresh to prevent token theft
- **Session Integrity**: Session metadata updated to track refresh activities
- **Audit Logging**: All token refresh activities logged for security auditing

## Implementation Details

### Service Layer Logic

1. **Input Validation**:
   - Verify refresh token format and structure
   - Decode JWT token to extract payload
   - Validate token signature and expiration

2. **Session Verification**:
   - Query discussion_board_admin_sessions by admin_id from token
   - Verify session is not expired (expired_at > now)
   - Check admin account status

3. **Token Generation**:
   - Generate new access token with 1-hour expiration
   - Generate new refresh token with 24-hour expiration
   - Implement token rotation for security

4. **Session Update**:
   - Update session metadata if needed
   - Log refresh activity for audit trail

### Database Queries

```typescript
// 1. Decode and verify refresh token
const decoded = jwt.verify(refreshToken, process.env.JWT_SECRET);
const adminId = decoded.adminId;

// 2. Find active session
const session = await prisma.discussion_board_admin_sessions.findFirst({
  where: {
    admin_id: adminId,
    expired_at: { gt: new Date() }
  },
  orderBy: { created_at: 'desc' }
});

// 3. Verify admin status
const admin = await prisma.discussion_board_admins.findUnique({
  where: { id: adminId },
  select: { status: true }
});

// 4. Generate new tokens
const newAccessToken = jwt.sign(
  { adminId, role: adminRole },
  process.env.JWT_SECRET,
  { expiresIn: '1h' }
);

const newRefreshToken = jwt.sign(
  { adminId },
  process.env.JWT_SECRET,
  { expiresIn: '24h' }
);
```

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **Invalid Refresh Token**: Return 401 Unauthorized
2. **Expired Session**: Return 401 Unauthorized with message to re-login
3. **Account Banned**: Return 403 Forbidden with explanation
4. **Session Not Found**: Return 401 Unauthorized
5. **Token Decode Failure**: Return 401 Unauthorized

## Related Operations and Workflow Integration

### Dependent Operations

- **Login Operation**: Initial authentication creates session and tokens
- **Logout Operation**: Invalidates session (client-side token discard)

### Sequential Operations

1. **Admin Login** → Initial tokens generated and session created
2. **API Requests** → Access token used for authorization
3. **Token Refresh** → New tokens issued using refresh token
4. **Repeat** → Steps 2-3 continue until session expires

### Parallel Operations

- **Profile Information**: Can be retrieved concurrently after token refresh
- **Permission Verification**: Admin role permissions checked per request

## Security Considerations Within Schema Constraints

### Token Security

- JWT tokens provide stateless authentication
- Token rotation implemented for security
- Refresh tokens have longer expiration but are rotated

### Session Management

- Session records in discussion_board_admin_sessions enable tracking
- Expiration times enforced at application level
- Admin status checked on each token refresh

### Audit Trail

- Token refresh activities logged for security auditing
- IP addresses and user agents tracked
- Timestamps enable security analysis

The system balances convenience with security by allowing extended authentication sessions while protecting against token theft and unauthorized access.

operations.description:
Upload a file attachment to an existing article on the discussion board.

This API operation allows users to add file attachments to articles they have permission to modify. The file will be stored in the system and associated with the specified article.

## Security Considerations

- Users must have appropriate permissions to attach files to the target article
- File types and sizes are validated against system security policies
- Files are stored securely with access controls
- All file operations are logged for audit purposes

## File Storage

Files are stored with the following metadata:
- Original filename provided by the user
- Secure storage path generated by the system
- File type (MIME type)
- File size in bytes
- Upload timestamp and metadata

## Relationship to Article

Each file attachment is permanently linked to its parent article. When an article is deleted, all associated file attachments are also removed automatically.

## Related Operations

- GET /articles/{articleId}/files - Retrieve file attachment list for an article
- GET /articles/{articleId}/files/{fileId}/download - Download a specific file attachment

operations.specification:
Process file upload for article attachment.
1. Validate article exists and user has permission to modify
2. Validate file type and size against security policies
3. Generate unique storage path for the file
4. Store file metadata in discussion_board_article_files table
5. Link file to article via discussion_board_article_id
6. Return file attachment record with generated metadata

operations.description:
Delete a specific file attachment from an article.

This API endpoint permanently removes a file attachment from the discussion board system. The file attachment is identified by its unique identifier (fileId) and must belong to the specified article (articleId).

## Security and Authorization

- Users must have appropriate permissions to delete file attachments from articles
- Only the article owner or administrators can delete file attachments
- The operation verifies that the file belongs to the specified article before deletion

## Database Operations

- The operation performs a soft delete by updating the deleted_at timestamp in the discussion_board_article_files table
- All file metadata including original_name, stored_path, file_type, and file_size are preserved for audit purposes
- The operation maintains referential integrity with the parent article

## Related Operations

- GET /articles/{articleId}/files/{fileId}/download - Download file attachment
- POST /articles/{articleId}/files - Upload new file attachment
- GET /articles/{articleId}/files - List all file attachments for an article

operations.specification:
Execute deletion of a specific file attachment from an article. This implementation handles the complete file deletion workflow including security validation, database operations, and audit logging. The system performs a soft delete by updating the deleted_at timestamp rather than permanently removing records from the database.

## Security Validation

1. Extract user identity from authentication token
2. Verify user has permission to modify the specified article
3. Confirm the file attachment belongs to the specified article
4. Log deletion event with user identity and file details

## Database Operations

1. Query discussion_board_article_files table for the specified fileId
2. Validate the file's discussion_board_article_id matches the articleId parameter
3. Update the file record with current timestamp in deleted_at field
4. Return the deleted file information including all metadata

## Error Handling

- Return 404 Not Found if fileId doesn't exist
- Return 403 Forbidden if user lacks permission to delete file
- Return 404 Not Found if file exists but doesn't belong to specified article
- Return 400 Bad Request for invalid path parameter formats

## Audit Logging

- Record deletion timestamp
- Store user identity who performed the deletion
- Log file details (original_name, file_type, file_size)

operations.description:
Create a new image attachment for a discussion board article.

This API endpoint allows authorized users to upload and attach new images to existing articles on the discussion board. Images can be photographs, diagrams, charts, or any other visual content that enhances the article's presentation and convey additional information visually.

The image attachment system supports multiple images per article, with display ordering to control the sequence in which images appear when the article is viewed. Each image maintains metadata including original filename, stored filename, MIME type for proper content-type handling, file size for storage management, and width/height dimensions for layout optimization and responsive design considerations.

The system supports the following MIME types for images:

- `image/jpeg` for JPEG format images
- `image/png` for PNG format images with transparency support
- `image/gif` for animated GIF images
- `image/webp` for modern web format with better compression
- `image/svg+xml` for vector graphics that scale without quality loss

When uploading images, the system validates file types, checks size limits, processes dimension information, and stores files in appropriate locations. The display order field allows organizing multiple images chronologically or by importance within the article's visual content.

This endpoint requires appropriate permissions - either the article's author or an administrator with appropriate access rights can attach images to articles. The system validates the user's authorization before allowing image uploads and maintains audit logs for security and moderation purposes.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new image record into discussion_board_article_images table with provided metadata.

1. Retrieve article by articleId to verify existence and get author_id
2. Validate user permissions (article author or admin)
3. Validate image metadata: MIME type, dimensions, size
4. Create image record with all provided metadata
5. Return created image record with generated id

Handle edge cases:
- Article not found (404)
- User not authorized (403)
- Invalid MIME type (400)
- Missing required fields (400)

operations.description:
Remove a specific tag from an article.

This operation allows the article author or administrators to remove tags from articles. The tag removal does not delete the tag itself from the system - it only removes the association between the tag and the article.

For article authors, they can remove any tag from their own articles. For administrators, they can remove tags from any article on the platform.

Security considerations:
- Authors can only remove tags from their own articles
- Administrators can remove tags from any article
- Super administrators can remove tags from any article
- Guest users cannot perform this operation

operations.specification:
Delete operation to remove article-tag relationship from discussion_board_article_tags table.

1. Validate user permissions:
   - If not admin: verify user is article author
   - If admin: allow operation

2. Find the article-tag relationship record:
   - Query discussion_board_article_tags table
   - Filter by bbs_article_id (articleId) and tag_id (tagId)

3. Delete the relationship:
   - Remove the article-tag association record
   - Use CASCADE delete to maintain referential integrity

4. Return success response

No response body required for this delete operation. Just return success status code 200.

Edge cases:
- If article or tag doesn't exist: return 404
- If user lacks permission: return 403
- If relationship doesn't exist: return 404 or 200 (idempotent)

This operation is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters should not cause errors. For idempotent behavior, return 200 even if the relationship doesn't exist. The operation only removes the association, not the tag itself from the system.

operations.description:
Delete a comment from an article.

This operation permanently removes a comment from the discussion board. The comment must belong to the specified article, and the user must either be the original author of the comment or have administrator privileges to delete any comment.

The operation supports the soft delete pattern where comments are marked as deleted rather than permanently removed from the database. This preserves historical data for audit purposes while hiding the comment from normal views. When a comment is soft-deleted, it remains in the database with a `deleted_at` timestamp, and the comment count for the article is decremented.

## Authorization

- **Comment author**: Can delete their own comments
- **Administrator**: Can delete any comment
- **Regular users**: Cannot delete comments they don't own

## Behavior

- Validates that the comment exists and belongs to the specified article
- Checks user authorization before deletion
- Updates the article's comment count after successful deletion
- Supports soft delete pattern with `deleted_at` timestamp
- Returns appropriate error for unauthorized deletion attempts
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Execute soft delete on discussion_board_comments table.
1. Validate comment exists and belongs to specified article
2. Verify user authorization (comment author or admin)
3. Update deleted_at timestamp with current time
4. Decrement article's comment count
5. Log audit trail for administrative actions
6. Return no content (204 No Content)
7. Handle edge cases: comment already deleted, unauthorized access

Security considerations: Only users with administrator permissions can create sections. Regular members and guests attempting to use this endpoint will receive a 403 Forbidden response.

This operation provides comprehensive section details including the section name, description, and timestamps. It allows users to understand the purpose and scope of each section before browsing its content.

This operation is publicly accessible and does not require authentication. Both guest and authenticated users can view section information. The operation does not expose sensitive data and is designed for browsing purposes.

## Database Relationships

This operation retrieves section information from the discussion_board_sections table. The section serves as a container for articles and provides organizational structure for the discussion board. Articles in this section can be retrieved through the related operation that lists articles within a specific section.

## Validation and Business Logic

The operation validates that the requested section ID exists in the database. If the section has been deleted (soft deleted), the operation handles it appropriately. No special business logic applies to section retrieval beyond standard database lookup.

## Related Operations

- GET /sections: Retrieve a paginated list of all sections
- POST /sections: Create a new section (admin only)
- PUT /sections/{sectionId}: Update section information (admin only)
- DELETE /sections/{sectionId}: Delete a section (admin only)
- GET /sections/{sectionId}/articles: List articles within a specific section

## Expected Behavior

When a section exists, the operation returns the section details including name, description, and timestamps. If the section does not exist, the operation returns a 404 Not Found response. Soft-deleted sections are handled according to the system's soft-delete policy.

This endpoint creates search index entries that enable fast full-text search across the discussion board. The search index stores both title and content text with trigram representations for fuzzy text matching, supporting efficient partial matching and typo-tolerant searches.

The index is used by the search functionality to quickly locate articles matching user queries without scanning the entire article database. Each index record references its source article and includes both plain text for standard search and trigram data for fuzzy matching capabilities.

This operation is typically called automatically by the system when articles are created or updated, ensuring search indices remain current with content changes. Manual index creation may be needed for backfill operations or data recovery scenarios.

operations.description:
Retrieve search index data for a specific article

This endpoint fetches the search index information associated with a given article ID. The search index contains the pre-processed content and title data that has been prepared for efficient searching within the discussion board system. The index includes both the original title and content fields, as well as trigram representations that enable fuzzy text matching capabilities.

The search index is automatically generated when articles are created or updated, ensuring that all searchable content is properly indexed for fast retrieval. This endpoint provides access to the indexed data that powers the discussion board's search functionality.

## Security and Permissions

This endpoint is publicly accessible - no authentication required. Any user (including guests) can retrieve search index data for any article, as the search index only contains non-sensitive text data that is already publicly available through the article itself.

## Search Index Structure

The search index includes:
- Original title text for title-based searching
- Original content text for full-content search
- Trigram representations for fuzzy text matching
- Timestamps for indexing and updates

## Relationship to Article Data

The search index is tightly coupled with the article entity. When an article is deleted, its search index is also automatically removed. operations.description:
Create a new ban record for a user.

This operation allows authorized administrators to temporarily or permanently ban users from the discussion board. When a ban is created, the system immediately terminates all active sessions for the banned user.

## Security and Authorization

This operation requires administrator privileges. Regular users cannot create bans.

## Ban Types

The system supports two types of bans:
- **Temporary bans**: Have a defined start and end time
- **Permanent bans**: No end time (effectively indefinite)

When creating a temporary ban, both start_time and end_time must be provided. For permanent bans, end_time should be null.

## Impact on Banned Users

When a ban is created:
- The user's active sessions are immediately terminated
- The user cannot log in to the system
- The user cannot create new content (articles, comments, etc.)
- All existing user content remains visible to other users

## Audit and Compliance

All ban creation actions are logged in the discussion_board_bans_admin_logs table for audit purposes. The ban reason is stored and can be displayed to the banned user.

## Related Operations

- GET /admin/banned-users - List all currently banned users
- PATCH /admin/bans/:userId/unban - Remove a ban and restore user access
- GET /bans/:id - Get details about a specific ban
- PATCH /bans/:id - Modify an existing ban

3. Validate that start_time < end_time for temporary bans
4. Check that the user_id references an existing user
5. Create ban record with current timestamps for created_at and updated_at
6. Set deleted_at to null (not soft deleted)
7. Return the created ban record with all system-generated fields

- The authenticated user's member ID (automatically captured from the request context)
- A reason text field where the user explains why they want to become an administrator
- Automatic system timestamp for when the request was submitted

**Authorization**: This endpoint is available to authenticated members. The system automatically captures the requesting user's member ID and does not require it to be provided in the request body. The member must have an active account status to submit a request.

**Related Operations**:
- `GET /admin/requests` (super admin only) - Retrieve pending administrator requests for review
- `PATCH /admin/requests/{id}/approve` (super admin only) - Approve a pending administrator request
- `PATCH /admin/requests/{id}/reject` (super admin only) - Reject a pending administrator request
- `GET /users/{id}/admin-requests` - Retrieve a user's own administrator request history

**Validation Rules**:
- The reason field must be provided and contain meaningful content
- Minimum length: 50 characters (to ensure thoughtful requests)
- Maximum length: 5000 characters (to prevent abuse)
- No HTML or markdown content (plain text only)

**Business Logic**:
- Users can only have one pending request at a time
- Users cannot submit a new request if they already have a pending request
- Users can submit new requests after their previous request has been processed (approved or rejected)
- Administrators cannot submit administrator requests (they already have elevated privileges)

operations.description:
Admin Role Management Operation

This API endpoint manages the administrative role hierarchy within the discussion board system. It provides capabilities for promoting regular administrators to super administrators and demoting super administrators to regular administrator status.

## Role Hierarchy and Authorization

The discussion board implements a two-tier administrator system:

- **Regular Administrator**: Standard administrative privileges for content moderation, user management, and section management
- **Super Administrator**: Complete system access including the ability to promote and demote other administrators

## Security Considerations

This endpoint is restricted to super administrator users only. All role changes are logged in the audit system for accountability and compliance purposes.

## Business Logic

- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator status
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator status
- A super administrator cannot demote themselves to prevent administrative gaps
- All role changes require explicit confirmation and are recorded in the audit log

## Audit Trail

Every role change operation records:
- Theacting super administrator (for accountability)
- The target user being modified
- The action performed (promotion or demotion)
- Timestamp and system context
operations.name: manageRole

Process admin role management operations for promoting regular admins to super admin and demoting super admins to regular admin.

The endpoint accepts a request body with:
- userId: The target user's ID
- action: Either 'promoteToSuper' or 'demoteToAdmin'

Implementation steps:

operations.description:
Report an article for inappropriate content or policy violations.

This endpoint allows users to report articles that contain inappropriate content, spam, harassment, or other violations of community guidelines. When an article is reported, the system records the report details and notifies the moderation team for review.

## Security Considerations

- Users can only report articles, not their own content
- Reporting is logged with user identification for abuse prevention
- Repeated false reports may result in account restrictions
- Reports are stored for audit and moderation purposes

## Related Operations

- GET /articles/{articleId}: Retrieve article details before reporting
- GET /admin/reports: List all pending reports (admin only)
- PATCH /admin/reports/{reportId}: Process report decisions (admin only)

## Validation Rules

- Article must exist and not be deleted
- User cannot report their own articles
- Report type and description are required
- Description length must be between 10 and 2000 characters

operations.specification:
Process article reporting with validation and moderation tracking.

1. Retrieve article by ID and verify it exists (not soft-deleted)
2. Verify the user is not the article author (prevent self-reporting)
3. Validate report type against allowed enum values
4. Validate description length (10-2000 characters)
5. Create report record with user reference, article reference, and metadata
6. Return report confirmation with generated report ID
7. Log report for audit trail and moderation queue integration

Edge cases:
- Article not found → 404 error
- User is article author → 403 forbidden
- Invalid report type → 400 validation error
- Description too short/long → 400 validation error
- Article already soft-deleted → 404 error

operations.description:
Create a content flag report for moderation review

This endpoint allows authenticated users to report inappropriate or violating content (such as articles, comments, or other user-generated content) for administrative review. Content flagging is a key component of the community moderation system, enabling users to help maintain a respectful and constructive discussion environment.

When a user submits a flag report, the system records detailed information about the reported content, the nature of the violation, and any additional context provided by the reporting user. This information is then made available to administrators for review and appropriate action.

Flag reports are used by administrators to:
- Identify potentially violating content that may require removal
- Track patterns of inappropriate behavior by specific users
- Maintain a record of community moderation actions
- Provide transparency in the moderation process

Note: This endpoint does not immediately remove content or take any action against the content creator. It only creates a flag report for administrative review. Actual moderation actions are taken through separate administrative endpoints.
operations.name: create

Create a new content flag report in the discussion_board_flags table.

   - target_type: 'article' or 'comment'
   - target_id: UUID of the target content
   - reason: Flag reason text
   - description: Optional additional context

2. Verify that the target content exists and is accessible

3. Create flag record with:
   - Generated UUID
   - Reporting user's ID (from authentication)
   - Provided flag details
   - Current timestamp
   - Initial status of 'pending'

4. Return the created flag record

5. Handle errors for:
   - Invalid target content
   - Missing required fields
   - Unauthorized users

   - Set deleted_at timestamp to current time

   - Log deletion action for audit

operations.description:
Approve an administrator request.

This operation approves a pending administrator request, granting the requesting user administrator privileges. The system will update the request status to 'approved', record the timestamp of approval, and associate the approving administrator with the request.

Administrators can process administrator requests submitted by regular users who want to gain administrative capabilities on the platform. Only super administrators can promote users to super administrator status, but regular administrators can approve requests for regular administrator privileges.

The approval action triggers the creation of an administrator role for the requesting user, enabling them to access the administrator dashboard and perform administrative functions.

This operation is idempotent - calling it on an already approved request will not change the outcome.

   - Set admin_id to current administrator's user ID

4. Log the administrative action for audit purposes

Return paginated results with metadata for audit dashboard displays.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of system configuration history records.

This operation provides access to the system configuration history table which tracks historical versions of system configuration with version numbers, configuration data, admin references, and change timestamps for full audit trail and rollback capability.

The endpoint returns configuration snapshots that include:
- Configuration version numbers for ordering and identification
- Complete configuration data as JSON strings
- Change reasons explaining why each configuration change was made
- Administrator information for audit purposes
- Timestamps for tracking when configurations were recorded

This functionality is essential for system administrators who need to:
- Review historical configuration changes
- Track who made specific configuration modifications
- Understand the evolution of system settings over time
- Support rollback scenarios by examining previous configuration states
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated list of system configuration history records

operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_system_config_histories table with optional version filter.
Apply pagination with configurable page size.
Include related admin information for audit trail.
Order results by version number descending to show most recent configurations first.
Return configuration data, change reasons, and timestamps for each history record.

operations.description:
Restore system configuration from historical snapshot.

This operation restores the entire system configuration to a previous state by applying a historical configuration snapshot. The configuration is identified by its unique history ID and completely replaces the current system configuration.

The restoration process includes:
- Loading the historical configuration data from the specified snapshot
- Validating the configuration integrity and compatibility
- Applying the configuration changes to the running system
- Creating a new audit log entry documenting the restoration action
- Invalidating any cached configurations

**Security Considerations:**
Only super administrators can perform configuration restoration as it affects the entire system behavior.

**Operational Impact:**
Configuration restoration temporarily interrupts service while changes are applied. All system parameters will be updated to match the historical configuration state.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Restore system configuration from historical snapshot by ID.

1. Retrieve the configuration history record by historyId
2. Validate the record exists and is not the current configuration
3. Parse and validate the config_data JSON structure
4. Apply configuration changes to the current system settings
5. Create audit log entry documenting the restoration
6. Clear any cached configuration data
7. Return success status with affected configuration areas

parameters.description: Configuration history snapshot ID to restore
parameters.name: historyId

responseBody.description: Configuration restoration status

access.description:

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring

text: I'll create the E2E test functions for the Economic/Political Discussion Board API. Based on the current state, the interface agent has been successfully executed and API specifications are available. Now I'll execute the test agent.

instruction:
Generate comprehensive E2E test suites for the Economic/Political Discussion Board API. Create test scenarios that validate both individual endpoints and their interactions, following these requirements:

## Test Coverage Requirements

### Authentication & User Management Tests
- Test user registration with valid and invalid data
- Test user login with correct and incorrect credentials
- Test password change functionality
- Test user profile retrieval and updates
- Test user account deletion
- Test administrator request submission

### Administrator System Tests
- Test administrator role promotion/demotion
- Test administrator request approval/rejection flow
- Test banned user management (ban/unban)
- Test access control for regular vs super administrators

### Section Management Tests
- Test section creation, listing, and retrieval
- Test section update functionality
- Test section deletion
- Test permission-based access control

### Article Management Tests
- Test article creation with attachments and tags
- Test article listing with pagination and sorting
- Test article search functionality (title, content, tags)
- Test article update and deletion
- Test permission checks (owner vs admin vs regular users)
- Test attachment download functionality

### Comment Management Tests

Test super administrator deletion of an article on the discussion board.

Scenario Overview:
This test validates that a super administrator can successfully delete an article from the discussion board. - All related discussion_board_article_images records are removed
- All related discussion_board_article_tags records are removed
- The main article record is permanently removed
- Appropriate success response is returned

- Only super administrators can delete articles (authorization check)
- Article deletion is permanent and cannot be undone
- All associated attachments and tags are properly cleaned up
- The operation cannot be performed on non-existent articles
